messages:
kevin: Heads up — weird behaviour in the SDK around tool/function calling + JSON mode + schema validation. Repro in the sample-app: we enabled structured_output JSON schema but when the model returns non-JSON the SDK just hands the raw text back instead of surfacing a schema validation error.

maria: Yikes. Can you paste repro steps / minimal request?

kevin: Sure, shortened:
```js
const res = await redwood.client.generate({
  model: 'open-rw-1',
  tools: ['create_ticket'],
  structured_output: { mode: 'json', schema: ticketSchema },
  input: 'Create a bug about login failure'
})
// model returns: "I made a ticket: see internal ref 12345" (plain text)
// SDK returns the same string instead of throwing/marking invalid
```

ajay: Hmm — expected behaviour would be SDK to either: 1) try to coerce/parse into JSON, 2) return an explicit ValidationError, or 3) expose raw + validation diagnostics. None of that happening?

kevin: Exactly. It tries JSON.parse, fails, but then falls back to raw string and we don't get any structured_error telemetry or a typed error. So the sample-app assumes the response has .json and crashes later.

jess: Could this be related to our retry/auth refresh path? We recently changed the auth-refresh middleware to retry the original request on 401, which could re-run the function/tool causing non-idempotent side effects and different outputs on retry. If the retry returns text but the first attempt returned something else the validation logic might be inconsistent.

ajay: Good point. I hit a related bug — when a token refresh triggers a retry we don't annotate the response with "retried": true in the SDK response object, so higher layers can't decide to suppress side effects.

maria: Two things to fix IMO: (A) SDK should surface a structured validation error with a clear code (SDK_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED) and include the raw output + parse error + expected schema; (B) add a helper like client.callWithSchema(toolName, schema, opts) that enforces strictJsonMode and returns { ok: boolean, value?: object, diagnostics?: string }.

kevin: Exactly. Also suggest an opt-in strictJsonMode that causes the SDK to instruct the model with an explicit system prefix and to fail fast if parse fails. Eg:
```txt
SYSTEM: Output must be valid JSON matching schema X. If you cannot, output: {"error":"UNABLE_TO_COMPLY","reason":"..."}
```
This reduces silent failures.

jess: For onboarding/sample apps, we should update examples to use callWithSchema and show how to fallback to human review for non-JSON responses. Right now the tutorial just calls generate() and assumes .json.

ajay: Also add telemetry: schema_validation.failure_count, schema_validation.example_snippet (hashed), and auth.retry_count_per_request. That will help debug production issues. Keep PII out.

kevin: Agreed. I can open a PR with tests that simulate: valid JSON, junk text, partial JSON (e.g., {\"title\": \"x\"), and retried requests. The tests should assert the SDK returns structured error metadata and doesn't silently hand raw string as the only return.

maria: One more nuance — some users intentionally want permissive JSON-mode where SDK attempts to fix common issues (strip surrounding text, extract JSON blob). We should support both strict and permissive modes. But default in SDK should be strict to avoid silent downstream crashes.

jess: +1. For permissive mode we can expose a helper that tries regex to find the first JSON object, attempts parsing, runs schema validation, and returns best-effort with diagnostics. But again, opt-in.

sdk-bot: deploy-bot: rollout scheduled for branch fix/sdk-json-mode at 09:00 UTC tomorrow :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ajay: Awesome. Action items:
- kevin: PR with tests + sample-app update (assign to kevin)
- engineering: add SDK error code + telemetry (ajay will own telemetry schema)
- docs/devex: swap tutorial snippets to callWithSchema (jess will update sample)

kevin: I'll open the PR in a few hours. Leaving repro here: https://git.internal/redwood/sample-apps/issues/324

maria: Thanks — this has been a source of onboarding friction (new users hitting silent crashes). Great catch. :+1:

jess: I'll add a tiny migration note in the SDK changelog so teams know to expect a new ValidationError and opt-in permissive behaviour.

kevin: Cool. If anyone wants to pair on the test harness later ping me.

maria: pinged.
